newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.

text.p: CYCLONE OFF NORTH QUEENSLAND
A Tropical cyclone has formed off the Northern Queensland coast while flooding is isolating towns in three states.
Cyclone Harold is currently 12-hundred kilometres north-north-west of Cairns and heading south-west towards the coast.
The weather bureau says Harold is likely to result in increased winds and rain activity.
Flooding has isolated Mt Isa in the State's north west, and cut road links to the Northern territory.
The southern border town of Goondiwindi has also been isolated.
In north-western New South Wales roads into the town of Wee Waa have been cut with the Namoi River expected to peak later today.
And floodwaters north and south of Alice Springs in the Northern Territory are being to recede.
CASA BOARD STANDING TOUGH
The head of the Civil Aviation Safety Authority, Justice Bill Fischer, says the Board is standing firm in the face of Transport minister John Sharp's continued attacks on its competence.
Mr Sharp says a yet-to-be-released report into the Falcon air crash in Cairns last year shows a major conflict of interest within the Aviation Safety Authority.
Mr Fischer says the minister's claim is wrong .. and a preliminary report of the full air safety investigation shows the crash was due to pilot error.
Mr Fischer's told ABC Radio it has nothing to do with his organisation's surveillance of the airline .. and the Board's position is unanimous.
UNION SEEKING TALKS OVER ARNOTTS STANDOWNS
The Australian Workers Union is seeking talks with Arnotts over possible mass standowns.
An extortionist has threatened to start poisoning Arnotts products from today in New South Wales and Queensland.
The company last week withdrew its products from supermarket shelves in both states.
Arnotts has stood-down some casuals at its Adelaide factory and has warned it may have to lay off up to a thousand full-time workers.
The AWU's national secretary Doug Cameron says he'll be seeking talks with Arnotts later today.
ABORIGINES CALL FOR ACTION ON JAIL DEATHS
The Aboriginal community wants action by State and Federal Governments as the Indigenous Summit on Deaths in Custody begins in Canberra today.
The summit was an election promise by the Coalition... Aboriginal Affairs Minister John Herron says he hopes the summit won't become confrontational.

The Chairman of the Aboriginal Justice Advisory Committee, Tauto Sansbury, says indigenous people continue to die in custody because the underlying issues of housing and education have not been addressed.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
